description: The twelve sacred Jyotirlingas are manifestations of Lord Shiva as pillars of divine light.

jyotirlingas.name: Somnath
jyotirlingas.significance: First Jyotirlinga, representing Shiva as the Lord of the Moon.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Chandra was freed from Daksha’s curse by worshipping Shiva here.

jyotirlingas.name: Mallikarjuna
jyotirlingas.significance: Symbol of Shiva and Parvati’s eternal union.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Shiva stayed here to console Parvati after Kartikeya left Kailasa.

jyotirlingas.name: Mahakaleshwar
jyotirlingas.significance: Shiva as Mahakala, the Lord of Time and Death.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Shiva protects Ujjain from destruction by remaining eternally awake.

jyotirlingas.name: Omkareshwar
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Vindhya mountain worshipped Shiva to attain greatness.

jyotirlingas.name: Kedarnath
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Pandavas sought Shiva’s forgiveness here after the Kurukshetra war.

jyotirlingas.name: Bhimashankar
jyotirlingas.significance: Shiva as destroyer of arrogance and evil.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Shiva destroyed the demon Bhima at this place.

jyotirlingas.name: Kashi Vishwanath
jyotirlingas.significance: Shiva as the Lord of the Universe.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Those who die in Kashi attain moksha.

jyotirlingas.name: Trimbakeshwar
jyotirlingas.significance: Embodies the Trimurti – Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Origin of the sacred river Godavari.

jyotirlingas.name: Vaidyanath
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Ravana worshipped Shiva here to gain invincibility.

jyotirlingas.name: Nageshwar
jyotirlingas.significance: Protection from poison, fear, and negativity.
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Shiva destroyed the demon Daruka here.

jyotirlingas.name: Rameshwaram
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Rama worshipped Shiva before crossing to Lanka.

jyotirlingas.name: Grishneshwar
jyotirlingas.associated_legend: Shiva restored a devoted woman’s son to life.
